moduleTitle: Performing API testing in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Describe the various API steps that can be performed in testing.
Review the steps to perform an API call in an individual test or in the context of an existing test.
Add an API validation step and configure its HTTP request method and endpoint.
Decide when to send an API request via the web page versus outside the browser context.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Two types of API steps: Add API Action vs. Validate API

elements.description: Used to get data returned from an API call — the data it retrieves can simply be used to check that something was returned (or extracted and used later), rather than asserting a specific value on the spot.
Used to validate data returned from an API call — usually validating data directly against the backend, asserting the response matches an expected value rather than just retrieving it.

elements.text: Both API step types support parameters in their documented fields. Choose action/validation for the required response use and assertions; parameterization is not exclusive to Add API Action.

bulletPoints: Add API Action: get/retrieve data from an API call (can extract or just confirm something was returned).
Validate API: validate/assert data returned from an API call against the backend.
Both step types support parameters; choose for the intended response use and assertions.

elements.description: Hover over the arrow where the step should go, click the predefined-steps icon ('M'), then choose Validations to add an API validation step to a test.

Choose HTTP method and endpoint, then configure headers, authorization, body and assertions. Named Basic/Bearer authorization overrides manually entered authorization headers. A configured assertion runs before additional response code; failed assertions prevent that code from running.

elements.term: Validating API responses against the UI
elements.description: Use supported assertions or additional code to compare response data and UI values. A quick Send preview does not execute assertions/additional code; only static local parameters are supplied and dynamic values become empty strings. Request retries apply to failed request status, separately from assertion behavior.

bulletPoints: Add an API step via the 'M' predefined-steps menu → Validations.
Configure HTTP method, root endpoint, and path in the URL field.
Validate API can cross-check a response value against the UI, not just the response alone.

elements.description: Browser-context sending includes browser session information such as cookies where applicable. Verify effective authentication, cookie policy and page readiness; selecting this setting does not guarantee every request is authenticated.
Outside-browser sending avoids browser CORS restrictions. It does not bypass server authorization, network access or all failure causes; configure the required authentication separately.

bulletPoints: Checked (default): API call rides along in the browser context, cookies included automatically.
Unchecked: API call goes out outside the browser, bypassing browser restrictions like CORS.

examPitfalls.title: Leaving 'Send via web page' checked against a non-CORS API
examPitfalls.trapDescription: An API validation step fails, not because the data is wrong, but because the target endpoint doesn't support CORS and the browser blocks the in-context request.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: When evidence establishes a browser CORS block, investigate supported outside-browser sending and configure needed authentication. An arbitrary API failure alone does not prove CORS is the cause.

examPitfalls.title: Only validating the raw API response, never cross-checking the UI
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Confirming an API response looks correct in isolation, without confirming the same data is actually rendered correctly on the page.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use Validate API to cross-check the API response value against what's displayed in the UI when the goal is confirming end-to-end correctness, not just backend correctness.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming only API actions can use parameters
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Choosing a step based on a false parameterization restriction.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Both types support documented parameter fields. Configure assertions and response use for the scenario, and test the actual request path.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How is an API validation step added to a test?

options.text: Hover the arrow where it should go, click the 'M' predefined-steps icon, then choose Validations.
It can only be created through a custom JavaScript step.
By editing the project's base URL.
API steps are not supported in Testim.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's added the same way as other predefined validation steps.
practiceQuiz.rationale: To add an API validation step, hover over the arrow where you want to add it, click the 'M' (Testim predefined steps) icon, and then click Validations.

optionExplanations.A: The predefined Validations menu contains Validate API.
optionExplanations.B: Custom code is not the only way to add an API validation.
optionExplanations.C: Changing a base URL alone does not add the step.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Logs confirm a browser CORS block for this API request. Which setting addresses that browser restriction, with server authentication still configured separately?

options.text: Check 'Send via web page' so cookies are sent automatically.
Uncheck 'Send via web page' so the request goes out outside the browser context, avoiding CORS restrictions.
Switch the step to a custom validation with no other changes.
Increase the test's overall timeout.

practiceQuiz.hint: CORS restrictions only apply to requests made from inside the browser.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Outside-browser sending avoids the confirmed browser CORS restriction. It does not bypass server authentication or guarantee that all request failures disappear.

optionExplanations.A: Browser-context sending does not remove the confirmed browser CORS restriction.
optionExplanations.B: Outside-browser sending addresses browser CORS while server authentication remains required.
optionExplanations.C: Changing validation code alone does not remove the request’s browser restriction.
optionExplanations.D: A longer timeout does not remove the confirmed CORS block.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What can the Validate API feature do that a plain response-only check cannot?

options.text: Cross-check API response values against elements shown in the UI.
Automatically generate new API endpoints.
Run the test on a different browser.
Skip authentication entirely.

practiceQuiz.hint: It bridges backend response data and what's rendered on the page.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Validate API feature allows validating API response values against elements in the UI, letting a test confirm the backend data and what's actually displayed to the user are consistent — not just checking the response in isolation.

optionExplanations.A: Supported checks can compare response values with UI data.
optionExplanations.B: The step does not generate backend endpoints.
optionExplanations.C: Browser selection is separate execution configuration.
optionExplanations.D: Validation does not bypass server authentication.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the main difference between the Add API Action and Validate API steps in Testim?

options.text: Add API Action gets data returned from an API call, while Validate API is used to validate that returned data (usually against the backend).
Add API Action only works with GET requests, while Validate API only works with POST requests.
There is no functional difference — they are identical in every respect.
Validate API can only be used outside of a test, never inside one.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Add API Action is used to get data returned from an API call (which can simply be used to confirm something was returned), while Validate API is used to validate that returned data, typically against the backend — they aren't tied to specific HTTP methods, and they're both usable inside a test.

optionExplanations.A: The documented distinction is response use versus validation.
optionExplanations.B: The step types are not limited to this GET/POST split.
optionExplanations.C: The guide distinguishes their intended response use.
optionExplanations.D: Validate API can run as a step within a test.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which statement about parameterization in Add API Action and Validate API matches the documentation?

options.text: Only Validate API supports parameterized URLs.
Both support parameters in documented fields; select the step according to required response use and assertions.
Neither supports parameters.
API actions need no endpoint because parameters create one automatically.

practiceQuiz.hint: Validate API’s setup explicitly documents parameters too.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The API guide describes parameter use for both step types. Parameter support does not establish one universal default; configure the intended request, response use and checks.

optionExplanations.A: Parameter support is not exclusive to Validate API.
optionExplanations.C: The API guide explicitly supports parameters.
optionExplanations.D: An actual endpoint is still required.

quickRecap.value: Retrieves/uses response data and supports documented parameters.
Validates data returned from an API call, usually against the backend.
Can cross-check response values against the UI, not just the response alone.
Browser context can include session information; outside-browser sending avoids CORS, not server authorization.
